Return this, allowing the call to be chained.

functions.name: LinkedListNodeInsertion
functions.summary: Dual-list node insertion. When a2 is non-null, a tagged 12-byte node (payload=a2, tag=1) is allocated and appended to a first linked list (head this+0x0, tail this+0x4, anchor this+0x8, count this+0xC). It then builds a second linked list (head this+0x10, anchor this+0x14/+0x18, count this+0x1C) of 8 or 32 nodes, each holding the base value *a2 plus a running stride of 432 bytes per step; nodes whose computed value is zero are skipped. The tag selects which value stream the node belongs to.

operations.description: If a2 is null, skip the entire first-list insertion section.
Allocate a 12-byte node for the first list with OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12); on success initialize node[0]=a2, node[4]=0, node[8]=1 (tag 1).

Append the node to the first list: if the head this[0] is non-null, point the old tail's next field (this[1]+4) at the node; otherwise set head this[0] and anchor this[2] to the node. Then set tail this[1] to the node and increment the count this[3].
Set the secondary-list iteration count to 32 when a3 is non-zero, otherwise 8.
Loop over the secondary count; each step computes the node value v7 = v6 + *v3 with the stride accumulator v6 advancing by 432 and *v3 re-read from a2 each iteration.
When the computed value v7 is non-zero, allocate a 12-byte secondary-list node with OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12); on success initialize node[0]=v7, node[4]=0, node[8]=0 (tag 0).

Link the secondary node at the front of the second list: if the head this[4] is non-null, set new-node next (v8+4) to the old head; otherwise set both anchors this[5] and this[6] to the node. Then set head this[4] to the node and increment the count this[7].
Return the loop counter, which reaches 0 after the fixed secondary count completes. Invoked from CollisionObjectInsertion (0x004B48E0) to build collision sub-list nodes.

unresolved: The meaning of the 432-byte stride and the semantic distinction between tag-1 (first list) and tag-0 (secondary list) nodes is inferred from structure only; the caller CollisionObjectInsertion (0x004B48E0) assigns the collision context.
The exact identity of the object owning this dual-list layout is unknown; the two anchors this+0x14 and this+0x18 are both set on first insertion, and the packet does not disambiguate their roles.

functions.name: ListAppendWithSubListGeneration
functions.summary: Appends a caller-supplied payload (a2) as a 12-byte node to a first linked list managed by this, then generates a parallel sub-list of 32 or 64 nodes whose data values are the first dword of a2 plus a 12-byte stride. Both lists share the head/tail/cursor/count layout: list 1 at this+0x0/+0x4/+0x8/+0xC and list 2 at this+0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1C. All node allocation goes through OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper.

OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12) allocates the list-1 node; on allocation failure v5 is forced to 0
List-1 node initialized: data = a2 (offset 0), next = 0 (offset 4), flag byte = 1 (offset 8)
List-1 append: when the head at this+0x0 is non-null the old tail (this+0x4) is linked to the new node; otherwise the head (this+0x0) and the cursor reference (this+0x8) are set to the new node
Tail (this+0x4) set to the new node and the list-1 count at this+0xC incremented
Sub-list data value v7 = v6 + *a2, where v6 walks the node memory in 12-byte steps from 0 and *a2 is re-read each iteration; iteration count is 64 when a3 is non-zero, otherwise 32
A sub-list node is only allocated when the computed data value v7 is non-zero

List-2 append: when the tail at this+0x10 is non-null the new node is linked to it; otherwise the head (this+0x14) and the cursor reference (this+0x18) are set to the new node
Tail (this+0x10) set to the new sub-list node and the list-2 count at this+0x1C incremented
Iterate the sub-list generation 32 or 64 times, advancing v6 by 12 and breaking when the remaining counter reaches 0
Return the exhausted loop counter (0 after the final iteration)

functions.name: LinkedListDestroy
functions.summary: Teardown of a singly-linked list container: walks nodes from the head pointer stored at this[0]. Each node carries a flag byte at node+8, a next pointer at node+4 and a payload pointer at node+0. When the flag is set the payload's inner allocation is released element-by-element (1016-byte stride, one EmptyStub_0170 call per element, driven by a count stored just before the payload), then the allocation header, the payload pointer and the node itself are freed via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Finally the container's four pointer fields this[0..3] are cleared to 0 and 0 is returned.

operations.description: Outer loop guard: while the head pointer *this is non-null, keep processing nodes.
Load the current node v3 from the head pointer *this and read the next node from node+4.
Read the node flag byte at node+8 into v4.
Guard on the flag v4: only flagged nodes carry an inner allocation to release.
Load the node payload pointer v5 from node+0.
Guard on the payload pointer v5 being non-null before dereferencing it.
Dereference the payload's first dword into v6.
Guard on the payload first dword v6 being non-null before treating it as an allocation pointer.
Compute the allocation header v7 = v6 - 4; the element count is stored in the dword immediately preceding the payload data.
Guard on (count - 1) >= 0, i.e. the allocation holds at least one element; otherwise the element loop is skipped.
do-while countdown over the stored element count, stepping the element pointer back by 1016 bytes each iteration.
Invoke EmptyStub_0170 once per element as the per-element cleanup.
Free the allocation header at v7 via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free the node payload pointer v5 via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free the node v3 via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Clear the container fields this[0], this[1], this[2], this[3] to 0 after the walk.
Return 0.

Semantics of the node flag byte at node+8 (why some nodes carry payloads) is data-driven and unknown.
The reload of the container pointer across FreeWrapper_7bcf calls suggests the frees may alias it; no further evidence.

functions.name: SessionStateReset
functions.summary: Session/vehicle state reset routine called per-frame from sub_4C6B60. When the global session type dword_7C56A4 is <= 6 (non-qualifying session) and the object condition at obj+0x32C8 (reached through the pointer at this+0x0) is <= 1, it re-initializes the AI racing line via AIRacingLinePathFollowing, downgrades the mode flag this+0x60 from 2 to 1, and resets the three float fields this+0x18/0x1C/0x20 to -1.0f. Regardless of those guards it unconditionally clears the status flags this+0xA8/0xAC/0xB0/0xB4/0xD0/0xD4, then returns the value read at entry (the session type, or the object condition when the guard failed).

Invoke AIRacingLinePathFollowing on the object racing-line subobject (object base + 12) to re-initialize path following.

Reset the three float fields this+0x18, this+0x1C and this+0x20 to -1.0f.
Unconditionally zero the status flags at this+0xA8, this+0xAC, this+0xB0, this+0xB4, this+0xD0 and this+0xD4 (a mix of dword and byte flags).
Return the value read at entry (the session type from dword_7C56A4, or the object condition at obj+0x32C8 when the guard failed); called from the frame-path ticker sub_4C6B60.
